scope: ValueBundle equality/idempotence after static elaboration and form resolution only.
problem: Historical set-like intent conflicts with v0.2 occurrence-local anonymous [] if duplicate elimination is performed on source glyphs rather than resolved identities.

models.reason: Deduplicating by source/structural spelling would collapse independent [] occurrences before they are resolved and can therefore change matching meaning.
Using AST occurrence identity as semantic set identity preserves provenance but makes repeated forms permanently distinct and defeats the intended extensional/idempotent bundle value.

Preserve source occurrences through interpretation, resolve every element independently, then compare/deduplicate by resolved L1 form identity. This keeps [] independent while allowing set-like order-insensitive/idempotent values once identities are known.
Multiplicity remains observable in provenance but is not currently selected as semantic ValueBundle equality.

pipeline: Static elaboration chooses ValueBundle before interpretation.
Each ValueBundle element is resolved independently using the ordinary read-only form-resolution context.
Resolution produces an ordered provenance list of occurrence -> resolved identity.
Semantic ValueBundle value is the extensional set of unique resolved identities.
Bundle equality compares those resolved sets; source order and duplicate occurrence count do not affect semantic equality after resolution.
No element may be deduplicated merely because its source spelling matches another occurrence.

historicalAnonymousIdempotence.reason: The two left [] occurrences may resolve to different identities. The equality becomes true only for resolutions whose unique identity sets are equal.

cases.note: This case assumes a statically Form-required context from the elaboration challenge; bare {} remains context-sensitive before elaboration.

nestedValueBundle.question: Does a nested ValueBundle remain a first-class collection value, flatten/union, or require a different construction?

expansion.reason: Expansion/query semantics depends on read-only memory indexing and must not be smuggled into literal equality algebra.

materialization.reason: ValueBundle interpretation and equality remain read-only; realize/delete are separate explicit operations.

passMeaning: Resolved-identity extensional algebra is coherent with occurrence-local [] and historical set-like intent for flat ValueBundle literals. Passing does not accept nested or expansion semantics and does not modify mts-contract/v0.2.
